props.title: What the five weeks actually look like
props.subtitle: The question behind most enquiries is “how much of my time will this take?”. Here is the honest answer, with what I need from you at each step.

items.title: One call, then a written brief
items.description: I send the brief back in my words. If I misunderstood the business, we find out on day two rather than week four. Your time: 60 minutes.

items.title: Two directions, not seven
items.description: Two genuinely different routes, each applied to three real surfaces. Seven options is a way of avoiding a decision. Your time: one 90-minute review.

items.title: Build out the chosen direction
items.description: Two rounds of revisions are included and scheduled, so nobody is guessing whether we are still iterating. Your time: two 45-minute rounds.

items.title: Handover your team can use
items.description: Source files, CSS variables, a one-page rulebook and a recorded walkthrough. Then a free 30-minute call 60 days later, because that is when the real questions arrive.

props.title: Three shapes a project usually takes
props.subtitle: Scope and duration, so you can tell which one you are asking for. Costs depend on scope and locales — I quote in writing after the first call, and I will say early if the budget and the brief do not match.

items.title: Full identity system
items.description: Mark, palette, type, application to three real surfaces, CSS variables and the handover session with your developers.

items.title: One focused piece
items.description: A poster kit, a pitch-deck system, a landing page, a packaging range. Useful when the identity already exists and one surface is letting it down.

items.title: Ongoing design partner
items.description: For teams with a system and no designer: reviews, new surfaces, and keeping the rules current. Rolling, one month’s notice either way.

props.title: The five things clients ask before signing

items.title: Who owns the files?
items.description: You do, in full, on final payment — source files included, not just exports. I keep the right to show the work in my portfolio, and I will hold it back until you launch if you ask.

items.title: How many revisions are included?
items.description: Two scheduled rounds per stage, which is what the estimate is built on. Extra rounds are €600 a day and I tell you before the clock starts, never after.

items.title: Do you work with in-house teams or agencies?
items.description: Both, and I am comfortable being the second pair of hands rather than the lead. I have worked white-label for three studios; ask and I will say which.

items.title: Remote, NDAs, invoicing?
items.description: Remote by default, two or three days on site if the project needs it. I sign your NDA without negotiating it. Fifty per cent up front, the rest on handover, thirty-day terms, EU VAT invoice.

items.title: What if it is not working out?
items.description: Either of us can stop after the two directions in week two. You keep everything produced and owe nothing beyond the deposit. It has happened twice in eight years and both times it was the right call.
